_about: The Pacific war's ties (ruling 197, the offer of war: the Pacific planner's paper 12, /mnt/project-files/pacific-planner/12-the-offer-of-war.md), read by src/campaign/pacific.ts and only while the far side's switch is on. 'power' is the country the ties are written for, which begins outside both blocs leaning to 'bloc'. It counts as that bloc's co-belligerent from the month it is at war with a member of the other bloc that is at war with a member of this one, and from that month 'china', at war with it since the first day, stands with the other bloc. 'pair': when the power is at war with one of the two and the two stand together in an alliance, the other is at war with it the month after. 'with': the countries that are at war with the power the same day one of the pair is, while they stand in its alliance (its dominions are world.json's, 'follow'). 'pact': the months from which Germany and Italy are bound to the power's war with 'with' (the far-pacific-war.json event 'pact-binds'): 'book' at the stops of the history dial that keep the book, and at the others so many 'months' after 'fallen' is beaten. 'freeze': America's sales to the power (and the south's) stop on 'book' at the stops that keep the book; at the others the month after the power holds one of 'places', and at every stop the month after it is at war with one of 'wars'. Once come it does not lift. 'north': the computer's 'nat' goes to war with the power so many 'months' after 'fallen' is beaten, while the power is still at war with one of 'while', and at the stops that keep the book not before 'book'. Until then the two computers keep the peace: no great choice of either names the other. The news lines are 'says' (the freeze's are ruling 197's own words, for the countries named here). 'demand' (ruling 199(e), the planner's paper 07): Japan may demand of 'of' the ground it holds that joins 'key' by land, while the two are at peace; the computer's Japan makes it in month 'book' while the book stands in 'theatre', and where no book dates it the month after the two of 'war' go to war or 'months' after 'fallen' fell, never once 'never' is beaten. 'keepers' (ruling 199(c)): who takes a fallen country's far ground into keeping, in order, the first still fighting the victor; its forces there stay and answer to the keeper. 'africa' (ruling 234(e)1): the list is Asia's and the Pacific's; on Africa's far ground, the provinces from the first to the last of the pair counted from the far side's first (El Aaiun to Sao Tome, with the towns cut out of them), the keepers are the wider world's own in their order, Britain and then America (world.json 'protector'). 'shores' (ruling 200, finding 2, and ruling 202(h)): the ground whose shores the Pacific's own rows decide in place of the second front's row: the 'slice' provinces of the far side's first slice (Pearl Harbor to Dunedin: Hawaii and Alaska, Japan, China, Siam, Burma, Malaya, the Indies, Australia and New Zealand) with their cities, and any province with a coast on one of 'seas'. A staff's own landing there asks the second front's own odds and risk (open.json 'descent'). 'skies' (rulings 184 and 187; the planner's paper 10, section 4): over each of 'seas' the air a side has is counted from its land air groups in reach of it, not from who holds the coast: the fighters of each group by how far its field lies from the sea's nearest shore (air.ts cover), its bombers in full inside their reach, as much of the group as its field can serve, divided by 'per' aircraft to a point, times the sea's air share. A resting group counts nothing, nor one whose field has gone unfed since its country's month opened; a group under a sky the enemy has won counts three tenths; carrier wings afloat are not counted here. 'cover' is the most a nation's land fighters reach for this job where the ruling gives one short of its escorts' reach (187(a): America's 550). The seas are the far side's, all but the western Indian Ocean's, where no groups are laid and East Africa's war keeps today's rule. The 8 and the shares are the planner's models: named for the tuning pass, not tuned here. 'runs' is America's shipping in the Pacific (ruling 190; the Pacific planner's paper 05; pacific.ts `pacificRuns`, read by world.ts and staff.ts beside world.json 'overseas'): 'share' of the country's sea lift works the Pacific each month on top of the Atlantic's, from the month it is at war with the power and not before (nor is it counted in the corps raised ahead before then). 'roads' are its two runs, parted by the 'equator' (the chart's own y: a harbour of the Pacific's ground below it is the southern run's, one above it the central run's). While the book stands each run has the share its 'book' rows give from their month on (the southern run all of it until June 1943, then three parts in five), slid with the Pacific's calendar; off the book the share goes to the road with a beach named for a hop, each road its 'both' when both have one, and all of it to 'idle' while neither has. When no enemy is left across the Atlantic that ocean's share is added to the Pacific's runs in their own proportion; when the power is beaten first the Pacific's share is added to the Atlantic's. 'from' are the run's own quays at home, the first of them in the country's hands with a way open (the port of embarkation does not change with the harbour named first, and no run of the Pacific's sails from the Atlantic coast). A run puts an army down only on its lane: a harbour on its side of the equator that the country itself holds, one on the home ground of a country under 'lane' (Australia, New Zealand), or one of 'havens' (America's own line, the planner's paper 14, section 4, point 2: New Caledonia, Fiji, Samoa, Port Moresby, with the New Hebrides between them); and a corps already across the Pacific is sent on by ship only along that lane. 'first' is the special formation (traits.json, 'unit') that sails on a Pacific run before any other corps. A player's America ships its own army.

says.beside: {Power} fights beside the Axis: it is at war with {foe}, and {foe} is at war with {axis}.
says.china: {China} stands with the Allies: {power}, its enemy, now fights beside the Axis.
says.freeze: America has stopped selling oil and steel to Japan.
says.freezeBoth: Britain and the Dutch have done the same.
says.freezeDutch: The Dutch have done the same.
says.north: Three months after {fallen}'s defeat, {nat} turns east and declares war on {power}.
says.demand: {Power} demands Indochina of {of}, and Vichy gives way: Japanese troops move into Saigon and Cam Ranh Bay, and the French garrison stands down.
